One-feature edit of PFGsteinitzbardeleben-5: the white queen on d1 instead of g4. Not from the game.

items.prompt: White to move. Find the best move.

claims.statement: 17.d5 is the engine's first choice at depth 16.
Qc4 is rated at least 0.9 pawns lower at depth 16.
Nd2 is rated at least 0.9 pawns lower at depth 16.
After d5 and the capture on d5, no pawn stands on the c-file or the e-file.
A white rook stands on c1.
A white rook stands on e1.
After d5 and the capture on d5, no white piece attacks d5.

hints: Look at the pawn on c6 and at what stands in front of your rook on c1.
A pawn move can give up a pawn to open a file for a rook.
Push the pawn from d4 one square.
items.explain: 17.d5 offers the pawn. If Black takes on d5, White cannot take it back at once, but no pawn stands on the c-file or the e-file, and White has a rook on each. The engine at depth 16 rates d5 about a pawn or more above the other candidates, such as Qc4 and Nd2.

feedback_by_move.e2c4: Qc4 is playable, but the engine at depth 16 rates it about a pawn lower than d5.
feedback_by_move.f3d2: Nd2 is playable, but the engine at depth 16 rates it about a pawn lower than d5.

items.prompt: White to move. Find the best move.

claims.statement: 19.Ne6 is the engine's first choice at depth 16.
Qh5+ is rated at least one pawn lower at depth 16.
After Ne6 the queen and the king attack the knight.
After Ne6 only the queen on e2 defends the knight.

hints: Black's king stands on f7. Which squares near it can your knight on d4 reach?
One of those squares is defended by your queen on e2, so a piece there is not simply lost.
items.explain: After Ne6 the knight is attacked twice (queen d7, king f7) and defended once (queen e2). A king cannot capture a defended piece. The engine at depth 16 rates 19.Ne6 well above the check Qh5+.

feedback_by_move.e2h5: Qh5+ is a check, but the engine at depth 16 rates it well below Ne6.

items.prompt: White to move. Find the best move.

claims.statement: 20.Qg4 is the engine's first choice at depth 16.
Nc5 is rated at least one pawn lower at depth 16.
Rxc8 is rated at least 1.5 pawns lower at depth 16.
After Qg4 the knight on e6 still blocks the queen's line to d7.
After Qg4, g6 and Ng5 the queen attacks d7.
After Qg4 the queen and the knight attack g7.
After Qg4 nothing of White's attacks the king on f7, so Qg4 gives no check.
The square g4 is empty, so Qg4 takes nothing.

hints: Your knight on e6 sits on a diagonal that runs to Black's queen on d7.
A piece placed behind the knight on that diagonal turns the knight's next move into a discovered attack.
Play the queen from e2 to g4.
items.explain: 20.Qg4 gives no check and takes nothing, yet it makes two threats. The knight on e6 guards g7, so Qxg7+ threatens mate. And any knight move now uncovers the queen's line to d7 (Ng5 is the one the game used). The engine at depth 16 rates Qg4 well above Nc5 and Rxc8.

feedback_by_move.e6c5: Nc5 attacks the queen, but the engine at depth 16 rates it at least a pawn below Qg4.
feedback_by_move.c1c8: Rxc8 trades a pair of rooks, and the engine at depth 16 rates it well below Qg4.

items.prompt: White to move. Find the best move.

claims.statement: 21.Ng5+ is the engine's first choice at depth 16.
Rxc8 is rated at least two pawns lower at depth 16.
After Ng5 the knight attacks f7, where the king stands.
After Ng5 the queen on g4 attacks d7.
After Ng5+ Ke8 the king guards d7.
After Ng5+ fxg5 nothing of Black's guards d7.

hints: Your queen on g4 looks along a diagonal that your knight on e6 blocks.
A knight move that is also a check forces Black to answer the check before anything else.
Play the knight to g5, with check.
items.explain: Ng5+ attacks the king on f7 and, by leaving e6, uncovers the queen on g4 against the queen on d7. Black answers Ke8, so that the king guards d7 and the queens could only be traded; taking the knight with fxg5 would lose the queen to Qxd7. The engine at depth 16 rates Ng5+ far above Rxc8.

feedback_by_move.c1c8: Rxc8 trades rooks, and the engine at depth 16 rates it far below Ng5+.

items.prompt: White to move. Find the best move.

claims.statement: 22.Rxe7+ is the engine's first choice at depth 16.
Qxd7+ is rated at least four pawns lower at depth 16.
Nxh7 is rated at least three pawns lower at depth 16.
The knight on e7 is defended by the queen and the king.
The rook on c8 is defended three times: by the queen, the rook on a8 and the knight on e7.
The knight on e7 guards c8 (and these other squares).
If the queen takes on e7, one defender of c8 is left.
If the queen takes on e7, the rook on c1 and the queen on g4 both attack c8.
Along the engine's best-defence line Rxe7+ nets at least a knight's worth of material.
At depth 16 the engine rates the position at least three pawns better for White, with Black's best defence to Rxe7+.

hints: Black's queen on d7 guards two things at once: the knight on e7 and the rook on c8. Count the other guards of each.
Capture the knight with check. If the queen recaptures, what is left guarding c8?
Play the rook from e1 to e7.
items.explain: Rxe7+ captures a knight that is defended twice, so Black may recapture. That knight also guards the rook on c8. If the queen takes on e7, it stops guarding c8 too, and the rook there has two attackers and one defender. The engine at depth 16 rates Rxe7+ far above the queen trade Qxd7+ and the pawn grab Nxh7. Black can decline: the engine at depth 16 rates every reply at least three pawns better for White, so the queen recapture is the line that shows the deflection.

feedback_by_move.g4d7: Qxd7+ trades queens, and the engine at depth 16 rates it far below Rxe7+.
feedback_by_move.g5h7: Nxh7 wins a pawn, but the engine at depth 16 rates it far below Rxe7+.

items.prompt: Same position, but White's queen stands on d1. White to move: does Rxe7+ still win material?

claims.statement: Rxe7+ is rated at least four pawns lower than the best move at depth 16.
Along the engine's best-defence line Rxe7+ loses material for White.
If the queen takes on e7, only the rook on c1 attacks c8.
If the queen takes on e7, one black piece still defends c8.
Ne6 is the engine's first choice at depth 16.

hints: Count the attackers and defenders of the rook on c8 after the queen takes on e7.
In the game, the queen on g4 was the second attacker of c8. Which pieces attack c8 here?
The queen on d1 does not attack c8, so only the rook on c1 does.
items.explain: With the queen on d1 only the rook on c1 attacks c8 after Qxe7, so the deflection wins nothing and White has given a rook for a knight. The engine at depth 16 rates Rxe7+ more than four pawns worse than Ne6.
